title: Aranya Devi Temple, Arrah
tagline: Maa Aranya Devi — The Forest Goddess of Mahabharata & Historic Veer Kunwar Singh Heritage

heroImage.alt: Aranya Devi Temple, Arrah - Aranya Devi Temple, Arrah

overview.short: Maa Aranya Devi Temple in Arrah is an ancient Shakti temple dating back to the Mahabharata era, enshrining twin stone deities who blessed the Pandavas during their exile.
overview.description: Located in the historic town of Arrah (Bhojpur district), Aranya Devi Temple is the presiding patron deity of the city. Legend holds that the town was named Arrah after Maa Aranya Devi (Goddess of the Forests), worshipped by King Yudhishthira and the Pandavas. The district is also world-renowned for Babu Veer Kunwar Singh, the legendary 80-year-old hero of India’s 1857 First War of Independence, whose historic fort at Jagdishpur stands nearby.
features: Twin Ancient Stone Deities of Maa Aranya Devi

overview.about: A historic Bhojpuri cultural center where sacred Shakti traditions blend with the revolutionary valor of Babu Veer Kunwar Singh.

howToReach.roadNote: Located 50 km west of Patna, connected via NH-922 (Patna-Buxar Four-Lane Highway).
